summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Transportation to ensure every state enforces sections 3 and 4 of Executive Order 14286 on commercial motor vehicles entering weigh stations by adding a new section 31152 to title 49 of the U.S. Code.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates enforcement of specific safety rules at weigh stations but contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any federal or state expenditures. It is a narrow directive on regulatory enforcement with no fiscal implications.
No provisions relate to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection of any kind.
The bill addresses commercial motor vehicle safety enforcement and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border security, or related enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights, abortion access, or restrictions.
No provisions address military or defense spending, policy, or operations.
No provisions address environmental regulations, emissions, or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The bill concerns enforcement of commercial vehicle safety rules at weigh stations. While it involves regulatory enforcement, it does not engage with criminal sentencing, policing practices, or justice system reform.
Although commercial motor vehicles are involved in freight movement, the bill focuses solely on safety rule enforcement and does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionism.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill concerns safety requirements for commercial drivers but does not address union rights, worker protections, collective bargaining, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination policy.
